subject: On‑prem maintenance window: staging rollout + fallback matrix
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: katie@acme-corp.com
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On‑prem maintenance window: staging rollout + fallback matrix

Hi Katie —

Thanks for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concise plan in writing for the upcoming Private (on‑prem VPC) maintenance so your SRE and compliance teams have visibility. High level: a staged, non‑disruptive rollout with a pinned fallback and an automated rollback path.

Proposed windows (your region / business hours constraints noted):
- Canary: 2027‑04‑20 22:00–23:00 PDT — 10% of serving instances in your staging cluster
- Stage 2: 2027‑04‑21 02:00–04:00 PDT — 30% of production routing (no customer traffic > 95% routed to warm cache)
- Full rollout: 2027‑04‑21 05:00–08:00 PDT — progressive by AZ, max 15m per shard

Key gates and controls:
- Version pinning: new runtime (redwood-runtime 1.9.3) will be deployed as a parallel variant; we will pin your production routes to 1.9.2 until canary health checks pass for 2 consecutive 15‑min windows.
- Health checks: token‑level synthetic pings, tail latency (<200ms target), and correctness checks against a short prompt set you provided.
- KV cache warmup: automated prefix rehydration for pinned segments; canary includes cache priming run after startup.
- Network considerations: installers require ephemeral egress to 52.23.114.0/24 for artifact fetch — confirm if your firewall needs an explicit rule.
- Rollback: atomic traffic rebind to pinned variant (v1.9.2) with rollback scripts that reverse kernels and quantization flags. Expected worst‑case failback latency: 30–90s for route rebind + warm cache penalty.

Attachments: I attached the detailed plan (acme_vpc_patch_plan_v1.1.pdf) and a rollback matrix CSV with step IDs.

Asks for you:
1) Confirm the three windows above or propose alternatives within the same week.
2) Confirm firewall egress rule or provide the change window for us to coordinate.
3) Anyone else we should loop into the canary approval? (Compliance evidence will be available in the shared Drive link.)

I will coordinate runbook rehearsals with Marcus and Vivek once we lock the window.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555‑0134

Attachments: acme_vpc_patch_plan_v1.1.pdf
From: Katie Rogers <katie@acme-corp.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-04-13T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem maintenance window: staging rollout + fallback matrix

Monica —

Appreciate the writeup. Quick notes from Acme SRE and compliance:
- Windows: the evening canary window is fine. For full rollout we need it to finish before 09:00 PDT (peak starts 09:30). Your 05:00–08:00 endtime is OK but please target earlier completion, so aim to avoid running past 08:30.
- Downtime: we cannot accept >30s sustained unavailability on any tenant during the rollout. Short degradation during cache warm is OK if recovery is automatic.
- Firewall: we do require a change request and will provision a temporary egress allowance — I will loop in ops@acme-corp.com for the CR.
- Compliance evidence: please include the canary logs + a hash of the runtime binaries and the signing cert (we need an audit trail).

Also: can you confirm the pinning strategy if a canary fails at 15% traffic (do you roll back to 0% or pause and keep 10% live for extended investigation)?

Thanks,
Katie
SRE Manager | Acme Corp
katie@acme-corp.com

> Hi Katie —
> 
> Thanks for the call yesterday. Per our discussion, I wanted to put a concise plan in writing for the upcoming Private (on‑prem VPC) maintenance so your SRE and compliance teams have visibility....
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Katie Rogers <katie@acme-corp.com>
Cc: ops@acme-corp.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-14T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem maintenance window: staging rollout + fallback matrix

Katie — thanks, good constraints. Answers below and an updated plan attached.

1) Timing: we will compress the full rollout to 04:30–08:00 PDT with a hard stop at 08:30. Each shard will be limited to 10m and we will parallelize across non‑overlapping AZs to keep within the window.

2) Availability target: our plan enforces a conservative routing SLO — we will monitor 1m P95 and a synthetic probe. If we observe >30s for any tenant, automated traffic rebind to v1.9.2 triggers immediately (engineer‑ack required to resume).

3) Canary failure policy: if canary fails at ≤10% we abort and rollback to 0% immediately. If it fails at 10–30% we pause, collect artifacts (logs + runtime hashes), and keep canary pinned at 10% for up to 2 hours for deeper investigation. If investigation indicates regression we rollback to v1.9.2.

4) Artifacts: we will publish signed runtime hashes and canary logs to the Drive folder. The attached PDF includes the exact artifacts we’ll surface.

5) Firewall: thanks — please confirm the CR ID and the exact IP range; we will not push artifacts until egress is allowed.

Internal note: Marcus, Vivek — please review the rollback matrix in the CSV and confirm the script IDs for automated rebind (RB001, RB002) and the warmup policy (WARMUP_A). Are we OK with the 30–90s worst‑case rebind latency?

I attached: acme_vpc_patch_plan_v1.1.pdf and rollback_matrix.csv.

Cheers,
Monica

> On Tue, Apr 13, 2027 at 11:45 AM Katie Rogers <katie@acme-corp.com> wrote:
> > Monica —

> > Appreciate the writeup....
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem maintenance window: staging rollout + fallback matrix (internal)

Monica / Lauren —

Quick internal signoff and a few implementation specifics before we send the final runbook to Acme: 

- RB timing: RB001 and RB002 are valid. RB001 (route rebind) is synchronous and observable via the control plane. RB002 (full instance downgrade) is our fallback if RB001 doesn't restore expected metrics in 6 minutes. Documented in rollback_matrix.csv row ids.
- Warmup: WARMUP_A will pre‑populate KV prefixes for the top 50 tenants using a prioritized seed list. That reduces cold‑start token debt but expect a short spike in token usage during the first 5–10 minutes.
- Network: confirm ephemeral egress will be opened only to 52.23.114.0/24 and artifact origins will be pinned to signed S3 URLs. We will include a verification step that validates certificate pins before applying the runtime.
- Observability: add a short‑lived tracing span for the first 500 requests post‑rebinding to detect regressions earlier than metrics windows.
- Compliance: we will upload runtime SHA256 hashes and the code signing certificate to the Drive folder; add a small immutable manifest file for audit.

I am comfortable with the 30–90s worst‑case rebind number; note the higher impact is cache warm. Recommend we ask Acme to advertise a short degraded mode to end‑users for 15 minutes post‑rollout to set expectations (optional).

If there are no objections, Monica — can you send the final runbook and CR ID to Katie and ops@acme-corp.com so they can schedule the firewall change?

— Marcus & Vivek

Attachments referenced: rollback_matrix.csv
